purpose: Change the masking predictor and the receiving learner separately on both external panels. Archived XGBoost/logistic outcomes on these tasks are already known; forest nominations and receiver outcomes have not been calculated. This is a prespecified learner sensitivity within the same previously studied candidate sets, not a new sample of datasets.
tasks: All ten first-panel tasks (30 folds) and six wide-panel tasks (16 folds). Use the locked training, proposal, guard and outer partition and exact ordered XGBoost Gain anchor and half-width candidates, including singleton no-action folds. Retain every planned fold; no parameter or seed search.
forest: scikit-learn RandomForestClassifier, 100 bootstrap CART trees, Gini impurity, sqrt(max_features) meaning sklearn max_features='sqrt', unlimited depth, min_samples_split=2, min_samples_leaf=1, class_weight=None, max_samples=None, n_jobs=1 and random_state=20421+fold. Refit from scratch for each support and training partition. Training-partition median imputation with all-empty columns retained. All other parameters take sklearn defaults.
voters: Archived XGBoost scores and new forest scores. For the latter fit the forest on all columns of fitting rows. Retain the identical original XGBoost-defined mask family and ordered support slate, proposal rows, training replacement medians, four panel weights, empty and restored anchors, relative metric tolerances, numerical slack and Gain tie order. Compute exact integer minimum vote, continuous minimum margin over the identical family, and empty first-panel margin for every candidate. Ties favor the first support in stored Gain order. Record complete per-mask panel metrics for the forest. Confirm nonnegative full margin iff ordinal vote >=3 for every candidate.
receivers: Cross each voter with the new forest and the two historical XGBoost and logistic receivers. For the forest independently fit the common anchor and every candidate on fitting plus proposal rows to predict guard rows, then independently refit every support on all development rows to predict the outer rows. Fit forests with the same fixed settings and seed. Keep each receiver's own anchor baseline. Seal predictions and forest selections for both panels before scoring outer receiver outcomes; no view of forest outer outcomes before locking. Report any missing run rather than replacing it.
decisions: Evaluate the same one-candidate guard with fallback. Report ordinal vote, continuous full-family margin, point margin, Gain and exact uniform; use 3% relative AUC and accuracy, applicable 5% relative average precision, 1e-12 slack as archived. Primary contrast full margin minus integer vote with forest voter & receiver, by panel; crossed learner results are sensitivity. Give guarded utility U, breach, accepted, AUC, accuracy, and task counts. Aggregate within task across all folds, then equal weight tasks. Paired 95% percentile intervals from 30000 resamplings of task differences, seed 33119.
ranking: For each voter and receiver, assess whether the same-family continuous score ranks successful candidates better than the integer vote on every fold with both outcomes. Use both the outer pass and joint guard-and-outer pass. Half credit for exact unrounded ties; average fold concordance within each contributing task, weight contributing tasks equally; give coverage and primary full-minus-vote uncertainty via the same whole-task bootstrap. Also count nomination changes, top ties, sign agreement and strict count-order reversals; the continuous minimum preserves the acceptance threshold but is not required to preserve all ordinal comparisons. Distinguish deterministic information coarsening, sample ranking quality, and realized guarded return.
runtime: Single-threaded estimator, progress and elapsed logged per fold, guard/filter and retrospective all-candidate costs recorded separately. If a single fold reaches one hour, terminate and report it. Count unique nomination masks, model predictions in rows, full/slate fits, and measured times.
